Latest Update: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
  • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
  • Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the firm that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, mentioned in a text ahead of the tech giant's after-market report on Tuesday.

Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    Recent findings suggest that the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    Recent findings suggest that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    According to recent reports, cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    Recent findings suggest that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

    Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

    The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Recent findings suggest that A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

    Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

    Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

    Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

    According to recent reports, safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

    By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

    It has been revealed that in fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

    They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

    Sources indicate that fresh managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

    He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

    Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

    In a recent development, due to his Burnley ties, newly introduced Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

    According to recent reports, after Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

    Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

    Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

    These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:.

    Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st.

    Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

    A debut for our brand new away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi.

    Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:.

    Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq.

    "We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8.

    "We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp.

    When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager latest to English football, it proved a vintage season.

    Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the significant question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

    Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

    “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

    “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

    Sources indicate that our experts have been having their say ahead of the fresh Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:.

    Sources indicate that it is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

    The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ.

    Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham.

    Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham.

    🔢 Team news...2⃣ changes✅ Kristi Montgomery & Andri Gudjohnsen come in🆕 Sam Morsy on the bench🤕 Augustus Kargbo, Dion De Neve, Scott Wharton, Moussa Baradji, Mathias Jorgensen & Lewis Miller on the injured list#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/esyE5Fibqc.

    ☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k.

    In a recent development, the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are fresh playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    Recent findings suggest that wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    Recent findings suggest that “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our substantial goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    It has been revealed that “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray mentioned. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

    The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

    During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

    Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

    Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

    Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

    Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

    After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

    According to recent reports, newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

    Sources indicate that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

    Recent findings suggest that bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

    Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

    Industry observers note that A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

    Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

    Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

    There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

    It has been revealed that elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

    Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

    Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

    According to recent reports, the striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

    Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

    Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

    The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

    Industry observers note that newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

    Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

    Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

    Sources indicate that time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

    Sources indicate that rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

    Industry observers note that leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

    According to recent reports, good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

    Sources indicate that bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

    Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

    Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

    Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

    Sources indicate that corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

    Sources indicate that jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

    Industry observers note that the scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

    Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

    It has been revealed that newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

    Sources indicate that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

    Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

    Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

    It has been revealed that that was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

    In a recent development, good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

    Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

    The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

    Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

    Industry observers note that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

    In a recent development, A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

    Industry observers note that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a substantial threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

    Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

    Industry observers note that newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

    Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

    In a recent development, leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

    Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

    There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

    Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

    Sources indicate that fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

    The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

    Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

    Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

    Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

    Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

    Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

    Newcastle United continue their preparations for the newly introduced season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

    In a recent development, new manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    Sources indicate that “It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle stated.

    “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about upcoming signings.

    In a recent development, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    Industry observers note that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he noted.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    #38731. The ‘Madden’ movie is a steaming pile of turducken

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (849 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    The ‘Madden’ movie is a steaming pile of turducken

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that madden released Wednesday on Amazon Prime, and it's one of the most confusingly stupid entertainment products to come out in 2026.
    • According to recent reports, the movie opens on the tail end of John Madden's run as head coach of the Oakland Raiders in 1977 at a time when pressure was on to win a Super Bowl after flaming out in the playoffs in four consecutive seasons.
    • Considering the significant setup this moment is given, it's almost alarming how promptly the movie then skips through the AFC Championship game against Terry Bradshaw and the Steelers, before giving approximately 90 seconds of screen time to Madden's victory in Super Bowl XI over the Vikings.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that madden released Wednesday on Amazon Prime, and it's one of the most confusingly stupid entertainment products to come out in 2026. It's a movie completely confused about what it wants to be, unsure of basic details, and feels thrown together in such a cursory manner that it's as if it was only created as a payday for those involved.

    According to recent reports, the movie opens on the tail end of John Madden's run as head coach of the Oakland Raiders in 1977 at a time when pressure was on to win a Super Bowl after flaming out in the playoffs in four consecutive seasons. It's established promptly that Madden is a brilliant coach, but viewed as incapable of winning the big one.

    Considering the significant setup this moment is given, it's almost alarming how promptly the movie then skips through the AFC Championship game against Terry Bradshaw and the Steelers, before giving approximately 90 seconds of screen time to Madden's victory in Super Bowl XI over the Vikings. It's a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment, that moves from the pre-game, to the celebration — with almost no football in between.

    Madden is not a football movie, though the sport dominates so much of the narrative. It's also not really a character study of John Madden himself. It's not a drama, nor is it a comedy — it just … exists. There is an astonishing amount of whiplash taking place throughout the movie, in which one second John will be having a dramatic scene with his wife Virginia over failing his family in service of Al Davis and the Raiders, then the next will be a moment of comedy between Madden and his fictional neighbor Vince, who is played by Shane Gillis, who does absolutely nothing to be anything but Shane Gillis.

    In a recent development, this back-and-forth between drama and comedy happens through the movie in such a jarring way that it becomes difficult to even focus on the narrative. None of that is helped by Nicolas Cage's performance, which is so horrible it defies belief. It's undoubtedly difficult to play a real person, but Cage's rendition of John Madden is more akin to Jimmy Stewart after oral surgery than John Madden. This is a cast full of incredible actors, but the only one who seemed to take the assignment seriously was Christian Bale, who legitimately turns in a brilliant performance as Al Davis, in spite of the script being a total mess.

    Industry observers note that in its almost two-hour runtime Madden takes us from John's time as a coach, through being lost in retirement, beginning his broadcast career, and into becoming the face of the iconic Madden NFL video game franchise. The issue is that it gets basic details completely wrong, in a rather alarming way.

    Comedian John Mulaney plays Trip Hawkins, the founder of Electronic Arts. We first see him on the field at Super Bowl XI, before he introduces himself to John Madden and Al Davis at a celebration afterwards to pitch them on his idea for Madden Football. Not only does this meeting make no sense, but it didn't happen. Hawkins was fresh out of college in 1977, he didn't have any influence to make it onto the field of the Super Bowl, and he sure as hell didn't meet Madden and Davis at the time. It wasn't until 1978 that Hawkins began a career in computing with Apple, and he didn't leave the company until 1982. It wasn't until 1983 that Hawkins first met John Madden, a full six years after the movie suggests.

    The artistic license of this moment is critical because it's not a side note of the story, but one of the primary conceits of the film. Getting these details wrong is astonishing, and calls into doubt most of the events shown. When Hawkins is rejected in 1977, Madden suggests he "ask Joe Montana" to be the namesake for the game. Montana did not take his first snap in the NFL until 1979.

    A technique the movie goes back to again, and again, and again is John Madden drawing up plays on the screen, as if he's performing a telestrator routine just for the viewer. None of these work. They're either overly simplistic for football fans, or confusing to non-football fans. They offer nothing outside of allowing Nicolas Cage to chew scenery and riff, never being good at either.

    We're left with a hollow, vacuous movie that seemingly exists only as a cash grab. There is no other explanation for how a director of David O. Russell's caliber (Silver Linings Playbook, The Fighter, American Hustle) turned in what feels like a rushed, lackluster, mediocre film devoid of any redeeming elements. If you want to waste two hours of your time just to laugh at Nicolas Cage trying to be John Madden, go for it — but there is nothing else about this movie that makes it worth your time.

    Madden is available on Amazon Prime Video, if you hate yourself enough to watch it.

    #38710. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

    📅 15 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2863 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

    📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
    • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
    • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    Industry observers note that manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

    According to recent reports, AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

    Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

    That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand stated everything you need to know about this moment...

    Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

    Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

    Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

    Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

    Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

    Industry observers note that united’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

    Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

    Four minutes of added time to be played...

    United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

    For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

    Sources indicate that martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

    It has been revealed that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

    In a recent development, big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

    Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

    Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

    Recent findings suggest that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

    In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

    Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

    Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

    Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

    For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

    It has been revealed that manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

    Recent findings suggest that milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

    In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

    Industry observers note that united have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

    Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

    Recent findings suggest that all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

    Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

    Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

    De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

    According to recent reports, manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

    The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

    Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

    Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

    Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

    United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

    Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

    Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

    United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

    A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

    Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

    A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

    Industry observers note that estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

    Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

    Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

    It has been revealed that milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

    United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

    Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

    It has been revealed that the players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely latest cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

    Industry observers note that we are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

    Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

    In a recent development, marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

    Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

    The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

    It has been revealed that carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

    So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

    Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

    Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

    In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE.

    Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha.

    AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos.

    Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda.

    Sources indicate that at his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his upcoming role. He mentioned: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    Sources indicate that “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

    “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

    Jul 24: Rosenborg 0 Manchester United 5.

    Aug 1: Manchester United 2 Atlético Madrid 1.

    Newly introduced signing Youri Tielemans handed first start as one of six changes to the XI that faced Leeds United.

    According to recent reports, our final starting XI of Tour 2026! 📋🤍ℹ️ Squad numbers worn in pre-season are provisional and yet to be finalised.

    Recent findings suggest that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

    Sources indicate that at the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

    Sources indicate that carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

    Sources indicate that kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, latest signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

    L'accordo tecnico c'è, ma Mizuno può pareggiare l'offerta danese, superiore ai cinque milioni a stagione.

    According to recent reports, lotito ha ottenuto una proroga per dilazionare le vecchie imposte degli anni del Covid, che pesavano per molti milioni sulla liquidità della Lazio. Secondo Il Messaggero, il presidente prova ora ad anticipare i crediti futuri degli sponsor e a inserirli nella documentazione per la Commissione, nel tentativo di trovare risorse per il mercato.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    La dilazione delle imposte alleggerisce un peso sulla liquidità del club. Il passo successivo a cui lavora Lotito riguarda i crediti legati alle future sponsorizzazioni: anticiparli potrebbe trasformarli in risorse da presentare alla Commissione.

    Il presidente ha cercato diverse soluzioni, ma non ha certezze e non vuole alimentare aspettative. Non ne ha parlato neppure con Gattuso, per evitare di illudere il tecnico.

    Per Hummel il discorso è distinto da quello dei crediti degli sponsor. L'accordo tecnico c'è, ma occorre attendere che Mizuno rinunci alla prelazione che le consentirebbe di pareggiare l'offerta danese, superiore ai cinque milioni a stagione.

    Industry observers note that la situazione resta quindi legata alla scelta di Mizuno. Lotito, intanto, mantiene il silenzio anche su questo fronte.

    #38693. How Damian Lillard has boosted Trail Blazers in promising return from Achilles injury

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2031 w)

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    How Damian Lillard has boosted Trail Blazers in promising return from Achilles injury

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The fear, when we saw Damian Lillard sitting there with a thousand-yard stare after falling to the ground early in Game 4 of the Milwaukee Bucks' first-round series against the Indiana Pacers in the 2025 NBA playoffs, was that we might never see him again.
    • Recent findings suggest that A ruptured Achilles tendon has altered, if not derailed, plenty of NBA careers.
    • What if that — that false step, that unsatisfying whimper of a finish to his time in Milwaukee, an era that felt like an error almost from the moment it started — was the last time we'd ever see Lillard looking like what he'd been for the previous 13 years: among the most dangerous shooters of all time, a generational scoring threat from the second he crossed half-court, one of the 75 greatest players in the league's history?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The fear, when we saw Damian Lillard sitting there with a thousand-yard stare after falling to the ground early in Game 4 of the Milwaukee Bucks' first-round series against the Indiana Pacers in the 2025 NBA playoffs, was that we might never see him again.

    Recent findings suggest that A ruptured Achilles tendon has altered, if not derailed, plenty of NBA careers. What would it do to a small guard with more than 35,000 NBA minutes on his odometer who was entering his mid-30s?

    What if that — that false step, that unsatisfying whimper of a finish to his time in Milwaukee, an era that felt like an error almost from the moment it started — was the last time we'd ever see Lillard looking like what he'd been for the previous 13 years: among the most dangerous shooters of all time, a generational scoring threat from the second he crossed half-court, one of the 75 greatest players in the league's history?

    An awful lot's happened since then: the shocking waive-and-stretch that ended Lillard's time in Milwaukee (and, more or less, Giannis Antetokounmpo's time there); his subsequent re-signing with the Portland Trail Blazers, the home he never really seemed to want to leave; an entire season spent rehabilitating and recovering, in hopes of giving himself a shot at becoming himself once again.

    (Hayden Hodge/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

    Industry observers note that "All the time off I had, I had to take advantage of it," Lillard recently told NBC. "Not just look at how far out I was and just try to chill or whatever. I had to make sure that every day counted. I was diligent in the process of my rehab, and then when I got back on the court, the weight room, making sure I was balanced on both legs. And then, once it got back to just hooping, that was the easy part — it was just a matter of shaking off the rust.".

    Fourteen games into his first action in 18 months, Lillard still hasn't totally shaken it all off and returned to the level that made him a nine-time All-Star and seven-time All-NBA selection. Entering Thursday's matchup against a Bucks team that now looks very different from the one for which he last played, he's averaging 20.1 points, 4.4 assists and 3.0 rebounds in 29.1 minutes per game, and shooting 39.6% from 3-point range — all at or near career lows. He's driving to the basket less frequently than he has since 2013; just 15% of his field goal attempts are coming at the rim, far and away the lowest share of his career. Nearly 60% of his shots, conversely, are coming from 3-point land — by far the largest share of his life in the NBA.

    He's had nights to forget in the early going, like scoring nine points on 3-for-13 shooting in a blowout loss to the Memphis Grizzlies, or finishing with nine on 2-for-15 shooting in Monday's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Those two single-digit performances, by the way, are already as many as Dame has had in any whole season since 2014.

    Dame's also had moments to remember, though. Like dropping 25 points with a half-dozen 3-pointers in 24 minutes on the Phoenix Suns in Portland's season opener, his first live action in 543 days ….

    … or knocking down a side-step dagger in the right corner to hand the Los Angeles Lakers one of just three losses they've suffered on the season ….

    … or punctuating a 13-point third quarter against the Oklahoma City Thunder with a vintage, swashbuckling just-inside-the-logo buzzer-beating pull-up triple over the outstretched arms of 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara:.

    "I knew he was gonna shoot," Blazers two-way guard Chris Youngblood told Conor Bergin of Blazer's Edge after the win over OKC. "I was like, 'If this goes in, this crowd is about to go crazy.'".

    Even amid the fits-and-starts with his finishing, Lillard has helped give Portland fans plenty to go crazy about in a pleasantly surprising start to the season — one in which he's been a lot more than just a nice story.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blazers enter Thursday at 9-5, in sixth place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's No. 8 offense and No. 9 defense, according to Cleaning the Glass. (The last time the Blazers ended a season in the top 10 on both ends of the floor: 2014-15.) They've taken down Luka Dončić's Lakers in L.A. and Nikola Jokić's Nuggets in Denver, swept a two-game baseball series from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder at Moda Center, and looked like a team capable of building on last season's return to the playoffs, ownership misadventures and personnel shuffling be damned.

    Dame's done it in part by working his way into a new normal — one in which he's no longer the sun around whom the entire organization orbits, but rather one component of a constellation in which All-Star forward Deni Avdija often shines brightest.

    Heading into the season, one of the main questions hanging over the Blazers was how first-year head coach Micah Nori would craft an offensive ecosystem that kept everything copacetic despite introducing two decorated All-Star on-ball playmakers (a returning Lillard, an incoming Ja Morant) alongside Avdija, who rose to prominence and helped return Portland to the postseason by becoming the league's highest-volume driver and establishing upcoming career highs in usage, shot attempts, touches and time of possession. The early returns were positive: The Blazers are plus-19 in 66 minutes with Avdija, Lillard and Morant sharing the floor, scoring a scorching 125.9 points per 100 possessions in their minutes with both Dame and Ja taking a smaller slice of the total offensive pie.

    In a recent development, the overarching experiment got paused when Morant went down with a hamstring strain, leading Nori to shuffle his starting lineup — first by sliding fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson into Morant's spot, and then, with Scoot struggling, swapping in 6-foot-6 forward Sidy Cissoko for a bigger, more defensively sound look. Portland's allowing just 106.5 points-per-100 with Cissoko on the court alongside ace defensive center Donovan Clingan and swingman Toumani Camara — a near-best-in-the-league level of point prevention.

    Recent findings suggest that removing one ball-handler from the mix has somewhat reduced the need for offensive sacrifice, but Lillard has continued to keep up his end of the bargain. He is finishing 27.7% of Portland's offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover — his lowest usage rate since 2014-15, when he was setting up LaMarcus Aldridge. His on-ball percentage — literally the share of his floor time that he has the ball in his hands — is the second-lowest of his career.

    Recent findings suggest that dame has never averaged fewer touches or a lower time of possession, spent less time operating in the pick-and-roll, or spent more time lurking as a catch-and-shoot threat option. Just under 19% of the offensive possessions Lillard has finished this season have come while spotting up away from the primary action, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking data — more than twice as much as in 2022-23, the final year of his first stint in the Pacific Northwest.

    According to recent reports, "Being on this team and having less responsibility than I had before, I don't have to make every play," Lillard told Sean Highkin of the Rose Garden Report. "I don't have to score every basket. I just came into this season mostly focused on how I could impact winning. I know that at the end of games, I'm gonna have to make shots and make plays and make free throws. But over the course of a game, I think the load is just lighter.".

    Deploying Lillard as a different sort of threat in a smaller-scale role has proven useful to the overall offensive operation for the Blazers, who are scoring like a top-five offense with Dame on the floor — and like a near-top-10 unit when he's on the floor without Avdija, which were minutes in which Portland's offense died last season.

    It has been revealed that last season, even with Avdija ascending as a downhill menace, primary playmaker and point-producing weapon, the Blazers finished the season just 20th in offensive efficiency, due partly to struggles with ball security (dead last in the NBA in offensive turnover rate, with 90 more live-ball turnovers than any other team in the league), shot-making (27th in team 3-point accuracy, 29th from midrange, 21st in overall effective field goal percentage) and half-court execution (just 29th in points per half-court possession). The arrival of Lillard has helped: Portland has turned the ball over less frequently, generated a higher share of its shots from 3-point land, shot better in the midrange, and scored more efficiently in the half-court with Dame on the floor this season.

    Even with Lillard not quite at the peak of his shot-making powers, his presence opens things up for the rest of the offense. With him on the floor, nearly 53% of Avdija's 2-point baskets have come via assist — 20 percentage points higher than when Dame sits. The driving lanes that were so often so congested last season are open a bit wider with defenses needing to account for Lillard, who ranks eighth in the NBA's gravity metric — a stat aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — just south of one high-volume superstar scorer in a ball-handling timeshare (Donovan Mitchell) and two designated sharpshooters playing off high-usage primary creators (Klay Thompson, Duncan Robinson).

    Industry observers note that that firm feels illustrative of the space Lillard currently finds himself occupying: not peripheral, still vital, but more of a complement than a centerpiece. (He still can shift into primary mode, though; on Tuesday, with Avdija sidelined by a sore left foot, Dame scored a team-high 25 points with five assists against the Timberwolves, pushing the NBA's No. 1 defense to the brink in a game that Portland nearly, and perhaps should have, won.).

    According to recent reports, plenty of superstars over the years have struggled to find comfort moving into that space. Perhaps due to the time away, though, Lillard seems to be navigating the shift fairly smoothly.

    Sources indicate that "Obviously, for the sake of rhythm and timing, you want to be on the ball sometimes, which I am," Lillard recently told Sam Amick of The Athletic. "But I think it just lessens the load of having to sometimes beat two guys, or get into the paint and do too much when we've got so many guys that can do that. I can space the floor, give guys space, and also catch and attack on the second side. It's been a process, kind of finding the spots, and it's becoming more natural. But it's been great as far as how I feel physically, how I'm able to play late in games, the effort and energy I'm able to give defensively throughout games. And I think it's a more sustainable way for us to handle the game.".

    Eighteen months ago, we wondered if we'd ever see Dame look like Dame again. While the jury's still out on that, what he's been so far — in terms of his combination of scoring and shooting efficiency, and by metrics like win shares per 48 minutes, box plus-minus, value over replacement player and player efficiency rating — nets out to something like a top-20 guard in the league. Just a month after coming back from one of the most devastating injuries an NBA player can suffer, that's not nothing … and, with a little more time, a little bit of luck and a lot more hard work, it's also not where Lillard's return is going to stop.

    "This early in the season, I still feel like I'm getting it back completely — just that rhythm, and taking bumps, and moving at the pace of the league," Lillard told NBC. "But I'm feeling better and better. [...] I've just got to keep it rolling, and keep doing what I'm doing.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Senza Zaccagni, Gattuso prepara Noslin sulla sinistra; Frattesi si è allenato in gruppo, ma resta il dubbio sul suo impiego.

    Andrea Pinamonti giocherà per la prima volta da titolare all’Olimpico con la Lazio nella sfida di sabato contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, L’assenza di Zaccagni gli darà ancora spazio al centro dell’attacco, con Noslin sulla sinistra al posto del capitano. Per il centravanti è un’occasione per cercare il terzo gol in biancoceleste.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    It has been revealed that pinamonti sa di non aver ancora conquistato i tifosi laziali. La fiducia di Gattuso nei suoi confronti, racconta La Repubblica, alimenta però la sua voglia di riscatto e può aiutarlo a sbloccarsi anche dal primo minuto.

    Nelle due precedenti gare iniziate da titolare, a Udine e Napoli, il numero 9 arrivato in estate non ha convinto. È stato sostituito nella ripresa, rispettivamente al 52’ e al 61’. Sabato spera che la prima partenza dall’inizio in casa segni un cambiamento.

    Industry observers note that proprio all’Olimpico, entrando nel secondo tempo, ha segnato i suoi due gol con la Lazio.     Industry News: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
