    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • According to recent reports, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the upcoming signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    According to recent reports, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    It has been revealed that first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Sources indicate that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta stated. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    Sources indicate that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It has been revealed that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Industry observers note that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    Sources indicate that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    Industry observers note that it should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Sources indicate that city, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where fresh boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    In a recent development, had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Latest York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

    Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    It has been revealed that prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    Shesterkin was a significant reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    It has been revealed that upcoming York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Fresh York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so promptly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

    • Sources indicate that LAS VEGAS — The Phillies are at a crossroads.
    • "We have a lot of high-end salary players, and they're not young, they're not old, but they're in that age bracket that you have to make a decision," Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowksi said Tuesday during GM Meetings.
    • With a likely lockout looming and the financial structure of baseball's future unclear, the Phillies have a projected payroll of $247 million for 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that LAS VEGAS — The Phillies are at a crossroads. A team that is still full of promise. A team that can compete with some of the best clubs in the league. A team that has World Series hopes. But also a team whose core consists of aging superstars.

    "We have a lot of high-end salary players, and they're not young, they're not old, but they're in that age bracket that you have to make a decision," Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowksi said Tuesday during GM Meetings. "Maybe we have enough high-end players, and we need to complement them with other players overall. That's a decision we have to make.".

    With a likely lockout looming and the financial structure of baseball's future unclear, the Phillies have a projected payroll of $247 million for 2027. Roughly two-thirds, or approximately $164 million of that money, will go toward players who are 34 or older, including household names such as Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, and Zack Wheeler.

    All three had quality seasons in 2026, but it's fair to question whether this team has reached its ceiling. Wheeler is entering his age-37 season, while Harper and Schwarber are entering their age-34 seasons. That figure above doesn't account for Trea Turner, an aging shortstop who will turn 34 in June, or Aaron Nola, who also turns 34 that month. Turner and Nola will make a combined $51.8 million in 2027.

    Sources indicate that "Right now we need an outfielder," mentioned Dombrowski. "You're talking about an outfielder, you're talking about some right-handed hitting, a utility infielder, a bit more in the bullpen.".

    Recent findings suggest that can Dombrowski do it all? Especially in a market and a game that is defined by uncertainty this offseason?

    "I don't know," he stated. "It might be hard because they all cost money, too.".

    Industry observers note that whether it's through free agency, trades, or both remains to be determined. If the Phillies do spend in free agency, Seiya Suzuki remains on the Phillies' shortlist of possible options.

    Despite the unpredictability surrounding the 2027 season and Philadelphia's financial commitments to aging players, Dombrowski acknowledged that owner John Middleton remains willing to spend if the right opportunity presents itself.

    Still, building from within provided a good amount of the tenor during Dombrowski's media availability. The Phillies' leader was adamant regarding infield prospect Aidan Miller, intimating that the 22-year-old is certainly a real possibility as a key contributor — even more so with the struggles of Turner at shortstop in 2026.

    It has been revealed that "I really am not going to ever anoint a young player a position," Dombrowski said. "I do think he has the capabilities, and it's just not me. Anybody that's seen him, and people from other organizations probably saying, 'Wow, you still have to earn the spot, but I think that, as it stands, that would be very helpful for us to have that consideration.' And frankly, I'm hoping he does. I'm not giving it to him. But I'm hoping that he does.".

    A fellow should-be NL East contender is connected to the best free agent on the market.

    In a recent development, left-hander Tarik Skubal will reportedly meet with the Mets next week. The incumbent Dodgers, according to general manager Brandon Gomes, have also been in contact with Skubal. The expectation is that those two sides will meet at some point as well, Gomes stated at the GM Meetings Tuesday. While other teams, including the Padres are expected to make a run at Skubal, the Mets and Dodgers are right now viewed as the frontrunners.

    The Mets are coming off an abysmal season, finishing at the bottom of the National League East with a 74-88 record. Surely the club is in need of starting pitching, posting a 4.47 rotation ERA, the seventh-worst mark in baseball. David Stearns, the Mets president of baseball operations, elected not to comment on the Skubal sweepstakes, a customary practice this time of year, but spoke around the team's needs.

    Sources indicate that "Having a complete rotation is really important, and that includes having pitchers who can successfully get you through a postseason and get you through a playoff series," Stearns said. "We've seen over and over again in the playoffs that that can be constructed in a variety of different ways, and so we're open to doing it in any way possible.".

    Skubal, certainly, would offer New York an anchor to its rotation. An ace that the Mets haven't seen since Jacob deGrom. But he isn't a sudden fix to all of the Mets' pitching woes. Unquestionably, talented depth also stands at the forefront of some of the team's needs.

    Industry observers note that the club traded Freddy Peralta to the Rays at the deadline after a bad first half with Fresh York. He turned a corner once he got with the Rays and helped lead them to a World Series. Also at the deadline, the club traded Clay Holmes, a converted starter, to the Cubs.

    Both pitchers are now free agents. Meanwhile, Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea, two veterans who have underperformed in recent years, are set to become free agents after the 2027 season (Senga has a $15 million option for 2028 that will likely be declined).

    Skubal is a logical fit in Queens, especially if Steve Cohen is ready to open his wallet.

    Recent findings suggest that "Every situation is unique," Stearns said. "It's been well-publicized, even since I've been here, we've engaged in extremely long-term negotiations for pitchers. We will do so again, but the situation matters. The specific circumstances matter. We do have to look at every individual pitcher on a case-by-case basis.".

    Corey Seager landing spots: Six possible destinations with Rangers veteran on the trading block

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that A new star-quality trade candidate recently barged onto the scene in Major League Baseball.
    • The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season, and that splash signing played a leading role in the Rangers' 2023 World Series triumph.
    • In a recent development, it won't be simple.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that A new star-quality trade candidate recently barged onto the scene in Major League Baseball. The Texas Rangers are reportedly fielding and considering trade offers for veteran shortstop Corey Seager.

    The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season, and that splash signing played a leading role in the Rangers' 2023 World Series triumph. Seager was named MVP of that World Series, and during the regular season he enjoyed perhaps the best campaign of his standout career. Now, though, with the Rangers facing an uncertain future, they may be looking to unload Seager and the five years and roughly $155 million left on his pact.

    In a recent development, it won't be simple. Seager is going into his age-33 campaign in 2027, and he suffered a downturn at the plate this past season (while still remaining a plus at the plate and in the field). As well, he's been injury-prone for much of his 12-year career. Over the last four years, he's averaged 111.5 games per season, and in recent times he's been limited by injuries to his thumb, hip, back, and both hamstrings. At his age and after such a long history of health concerns, there's no reason to think that will change. Additionally, Seager can control the process. While his contract included a limited no-trade clause that allowed him to block trades to eight teams of his choosing, Seager has now earned "10 and 5" rights – i.e., he's spent at least 10 seasons in the majors and the last five with the same team – which means he has the right to block any trade.

    All that said, Seager is no doubt appealing to teams in contending mode and in need of upgrades on the left side of the infield. He still has strong quality-of-contact indicators at the plate, and he's still an asset with the glove. It's easy to dream on that career OPS+ of 135 from the shortstop position and the fact that he was at peak, at least when he was on the field, as recently as 2025. The Rangers are also presumably willing to pay down a chunk of his remaining commitment in order to make a trade more tenable. As for Seager's druthers, it's possible he'd like to play out his contract for a team better positioned to deliver to him a third career World Series ring.

    With all those considerations laid out, let's have a look at a handful of teams who may – or at least should – be kicking the tires on a Seager trade. We'll proceed in taut and suspenseful alphabetical order ….

    Sources indicate that the Braves made it to the NLDS this past season and have made the playoffs in eight of the last nine years. For much of that time, though, they've struggled to find a reliable presence at shortstop. This past season, Atlanta shortstops combined to bat just .222/.280/.322, which is squarely in "unacceptable liability" territory. As well, the top two turn-takers at the position, Mauricio Dubón and Ha-Seong Kim, are both free agents.

    According to recent reports, boston still has Trevor Story under contract through next season with a club option for 2028. However, Story, who soon turns 34, appears to be very much in decline, and that's in addition to his troubles staying healthy. This past season, he had an OPS+ of just 75 and was barely above replacement level overall. The Sox have signaled they're open to an upgrade at the position, and Seager would certainly be that.

    Why not a headline-grabbing reunion in L.A.? Seager was a Dodgers lifer before he inked that big contract with Texas, and that level of familiarity – plus the Dodgers' ongoing excellence – could be alluring. The Dodgers could also use an upgrade in the middle infield. They could install Seager at short and shift Mookie Betts to second base, where he has significant experience. Or they could keep Betts at short, where he's adapted so very well, and let Seager transition to second – a marginally less taxing position that might even help him stay on the field. Tommy Edman, meanwhile, would transition back to a super-utility role. Either way, it's a compelling theoretical fit.

    The Yankees have previously shown trade interest in Seager, so it's no great leap to think they still might be eyeing him from afar. Young George Lombard Jr. is the shortstop of the present and future in the Bronx, so Seager would likely need to be willing to shift to third base if a Yankees trade is to come to pass. The Yanks have already signaled they're ready for an upgrade over Ryan McMahon, who's been frankly terrible at the plate since being acquired from the Rockies. The lefty-swinging Seager doubtless would enjoy that short porch in right at Yankee Stadium.

    Trea Turner is signed through 2033, but defensively he's become unplayable at the shortstop position. No surprise, then, that the Phillies are open to moving him, perhaps to the outfield, and finding someone else to man the critical position of short. Seager would be a needle-moving addition for lead operator Dave Dombrowski as he attempts to keep the Phils' contending window open for a bit longer. There's an argument that this would make the Philly lineup too left-handed, but the potential upgrade over what Turner provided them this past season makes it a worthwhile sacrifice.

    The Jays had one of the worst offenses in all of baseball last season, and that lack of punch was the leading culprit in their tumble from the heights of 2025. Seager could be installed at short or second, and from there the Jays could shuffle infield incumbents Andrés Giménez and Ernie Clement. Indeed, Clement is perhaps at his most valuable when he's deployed as a heavily used multi-positional talent.

    • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • Recent findings suggest that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace and the ongoing GM Meetings, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • The Red Sox are once again shopping outfielder Jarren Duran, reports the Boston Globe.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 1 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22. As for the present moment, the General Manager Meetings in Las Vegas are underway, and since there may not be any Winter Meetings this offseason (thanks to the lockout), the GMs' pow-wow could instead be a locus of activity.

    Recent findings suggest that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace and the ongoing GM Meetings, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Wednesday's supply just below.

    The Red Sox are once again shopping outfielder Jarren Duran, reports the Boston Globe. He has been in trade rumors constantly the last two years or so. Boston has also reportedly shown interest in free agent Seiya Suzuki, the best right-handed bat on the market. With Gold Glover Wilyer Abreu entrenched in right, the Red Sox would presumably use Suzuki in left field or DH.

    Recent findings suggest that duran, 30, has two years of team control remaining and he's a possible buy-low candidate. From 2023-25, he authored a .276/.339/.471 batting line with 17 homers and 32 steals per season. He slipped to .207/.266/.361 in 2026, however, and the Red Sox need to add power and get more right-handed. Moving Duran to clear a spot for Suzuki would address both needs.

    Industry observers note that the Upcoming York Yankees are eyeing an upgrade at third base given the prolonged struggles of Ryan McMahon, and free agent Alec Bohm may be a potential target for GM Brian Cashman, according to the New York Post. Bohm, 30, is coming off a subpar walk year for the Philadelphia Phillies, but he has a career OPS+ of 101 overall. He also fared much better in the second half, and his season-long numbers were dragged down by a terrible April. Bohm is not much of a fielder these days, but the Yankees may be willing to live with that if they determine he can provide an offensive upgrade.

    As for McMahon, Cashman already conceded to looking for a replacement.

    "He's signed through next year for us, but I definitely know we need to improve production in a lot of different spots on the club if we can," he told reporters on Tuesday. "So we'll be open-minded to finding what we can run into if it's there.".

    The market for ace Tarik Skubal, far and away the top free agent available this offseason, continues to pick up steam, and it may be that he signs his next contract before the owners lock out the players on Dec. 1. The Los Angeles Dodgers, who traded for Skubal leading up to the deadline, the New York Mets, the Chicago Cubs, and the San Diego Padres are known to have varying levels of interest in Skubal. Now, the New York Post reports, the Toronto Blue Jays have entered the fray and emerged as Skubal suitors.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the Dodgers, they indeed plan to meet with Skubal, GM Brandon Gomes stated. There could be a twist in their pursuit, though; The Athletic reports that the Dodgers are interested in Skubal on a short-term deal, presumably with a higher AAV like they gave to Kyle Tucker. But given the uncertainty of the CBA, would Skubal be willing to sign a contract that has him back on the market in just a few years?

    Mets top executive David Stearns, meanwhile, emphasized on Tuesday that he and the club are willing to offer lengthy contracts to pitchers but that circumstances matter. That, in theory, should allay fears that he's not prepared to make a significant offer.

    The San Diego Padres not long ago declined their club option on right-handed starter Nick Pivetta. However, they may not mean a parting of ways for club and player. Padres lead decision-maker AJ Preller on Tuesday told reporters, including Marty Caswell, that the team hopes to work out a upcoming agreement with Pivetta so that he can return to San Diego for the 2027 season and perhaps beyond. Pivetta enjoyed a standout season in 2025, but his 2026, while excellent while on the mound, consisted of just eight regular-season starts because of elbow problems.

    It has been revealed that dylan Crews, the 24-year-old outfielder for the Washington Nationals, has yet to reach the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2023. However, that ceiling is still there, and Crews is obviously young enough to realize his promise. Speaking of Crews, the Athletic reports that multiple teams have approached the Nats about Crews' availability in trade and that the Nats have not declared him off-limits. That of course doesn't mean a trade will happen, but a change of scenery for Crews may indeed be a winter possibility.

    Industry observers note that outfielder Randy Arozarena was the Seattle Mariners' top player last season, and now he's a free agent. The M's, though, may not be interested in bringing back Arozarena and instead may be targeting fellow free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki, the Seattle Times reports. Each veteran outfielder will be going into his age-32 season in 2027, and each produced at a high level in 2026.

    According to recent reports, after missing the playoffs in back-to-back seasons and trading away catcher Adley Rutschman leading up to the 2026 deadline, the Baltimore Orioles seem like a teardown candidate on paper. However, president of baseball operations Mike Elias batted down talk of a major roster makeover. "A lot of our key, core players are very unlikely to go anywhere," Elias told the media, including the Baltimore Banner, at the GM Meetings.

    That presumably means that coveted shortstop Gunnar Henderson, among other notable names, won't be going anywhere this winter.

    According to recent reports, new York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler is the winner of the American League Cy Young Award for 2026. Schlittler was a unanimous selection via the Baseball Writers Association of America balloting, the results of which were revealed on Wednesday, beating out Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease and Guardians rookie Parker Messick.

    Schlittler's win snapped the run of free agent Tarik Skubal, who won the last two AL Cy Youngs as a member of the Detroit Tigers.

    This past season, the right-handed Schlitter in his age-25 campaign put up dominant numbers:.

    In addition to the above, Schlitter led AL pitchers in WAR with a mark of 7.0, and his ERA+ of 215 also paced his league. That 215 ERA+, which means that Schlittler's park-adjusted ERA was 115% better than the league average, is a Yankees franchise record. Among Yankee qualifiers, only Ron Guidry's 208 in 1978 comes close. Additionally, Schlittler tied for the AL lead this season with an FIP of 2.56, and he struck out 31.4% of opposing batters, which also ranked second in the AL.

    According to recent reports, without Schlittler's top-shelf contributions, the Yankees, without franchise slugger and reigning back-to-back AL MVP Aaron Judge for almost 100 games, might have struggled to make the postseason. Instead, Schlittler's excellence at the front of the rotation helped them win 93 games, post the AL's top run differential, and advance to the ALDS.

    "Cam had as dominant a season as a starting pitcher can have from start to finish," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said in a statement. "He's shown an astonishing amount of growth since we drafted him, and his success is no accident. Cam has a tireless appetite for hard work and refinement that has allowed his talents to truly flourish. This Cy Young is richly deserved. Cam was the most dominant pitcher in our league and continues to grow into a foundational player for this franchise.".

    While Schlittler was outstanding as a rookie in 2025, this past season, he increased usage of his sinker and cutter and improved ride on his 98-mph fastball helped him take the next step and become one of the very pitchers in all of baseball. Since Schlittler doesn't turn 26 until February, continued dominance may be on the way.

    According to recent reports, schlittler is now the seventh Yankee to win the Cy Young Award. He joins teammate Gerrit Cole in 2023, Roger Clemens in 2001, Guidry in 1978, Sparky Lyle in 1977, Whitey Ford in 1961, and Bob Turley in 1958.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko.     Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    In a recent development, look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    In a recent development, steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    It has been revealed that finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an matter is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
    • “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
    • Recent findings suggest that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

    “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

    Recent findings suggest that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

    Sources indicate that as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

    “They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

    Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

    Industry observers note that “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they highlighted it,” Lampard mentioned. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

    "They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

    Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he remarked, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

    If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

    The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment latest signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

    The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

    Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

    Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the fresh £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

    It has been revealed that "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

    From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

    "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

    "I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

    According to recent reports, it’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

    Recent findings suggest that FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

    There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

    Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

    Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

    Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

    Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

    Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

    Industry observers note that odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

    Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

    In a recent development, lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

    Industry observers note that here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

    Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

    The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

    Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his latest side.

    Sources indicate that odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

    Industry observers note that the ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

    From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

    Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

    According to recent reports, it’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

    Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

    Industry observers note that white overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

    According to recent reports, it's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

    According to recent reports, odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

    Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/.

    In a recent development, we are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

    It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

    Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

    According to recent reports, once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

    Week 11 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys have been bad, but their season isn't dead yet

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • No matter what happens with the Dallas Cowboys, good or bad, there will be an overreaction.
    • Recent findings suggest that you'd think, based on the commentary, that the Cowboys are hopelessly finished for this 2027 NFL season.
    • But the reality is, the Cowboys aren't finished this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    No matter what happens with the Dallas Cowboys, good or bad, there will be an overreaction.

    Recent findings suggest that you'd think, based on the commentary, that the Cowboys are hopelessly finished for this 2027 NFL season. And the criticism of the defense has been fair. That group has been awful all season, and reached a low point in allowing 584 yards and 46 points to the 49ers last week.

    But the reality is, the Cowboys aren't finished this season.

    According to recent reports, the move to demote defensive coordinator Christian Parker and have Mike Pettine call plays is probably a few weeks too late, but at least it happened. Perhaps nobody can save the Cowboys' defense, but maybe it works. Parker was overwhelmed in his first season coordinating a defense. Pettine has good experience in the role.

    And, more importantly to the big picture and where Dallas' season might be headed, the Cowboys play in the NFC East.

    Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys have had a rough start to this season.

    It's reasonable to think the Cowboys can't rally, no matter how bad their division is. Dallas is a major reason the NFC East has been a laughingstock of the NFL season. But at 4-6, the Cowboys are not out of range from the 5-3-1 Giants. The Giants are nearly a touchdown underdog this week vs. the Jaguars and the Cowboys are favored over the Tennessee Titans by 7.5 points. If the favorites win in those games, the Cowboys are back in it. Then, Dallas gets the depleted Eagles on Thanksgiving. It's not too much to ask for them to be back to .500 heading into December. DVOA has Dallas with a 32.1% chance to make the playoffs.

    So it's not impossible for the Cowboys to make the playoffs, which would be preposterous based on how bad their defense has been, but the division hasn't run away from them. Still, laying 7.5 points to the Titans might be too much. Cam Ward might be turning a corner; he has played well the past two weeks with the Titans giving him more control over the offense at the line of scrimmage. At the very least, Pettine is unlikely to completely fix Dallas' defense in one week. The Titans have been competitive lately, and that's why Tennessee +7.5 is the pick. But even with a close win over the 1-8 Titans, Dallas really will feel like it is alive again this season. And there will be an overreaction to that, as usual.

    Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 11 of the NFL season:.

    Sources indicate that let's establish this: Nobody wants to pick the 2026 Colts the rest of this season. But the Texans are very disappointing and that's a lot of points to lay for a 3-6 team. Let's just move on.

    Recent findings suggest that oddsmakers are still confident in the Lions. Detroit has heavy -525 odds to make the playoffs. That makes some sense because the Lions are 7-2 and a very good offensive team. But can the defense get by without defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell? It wasn't a good defense before those injuries (though it has been better since safety Brian Branch returned). It's worth testing Detroit by taking a Buccaneers team that was on a bye last week while the Lions were in Germany.

    We've reached the point in the season where some of the worst teams are not competitive. Five of the 13 games this week have double-digit spreads, with the two largest spreads of the season. This is one of them. Whenever you take a double-digit underdog in the NFL, it seems like a horrible idea (see: Colts on Thursday). Who wants to spend an afternoon backing Carson Beck at Arrowhead Stadium? But oddsmakers know this and you're not getting any value on the Chiefs. So, if you're in the practice of picking every NFL game against the spread, suck it up and back those big underdogs.

    According to recent reports, and here's the biggest spread of the season to date. The Dolphins do fight hard and Kyle McCord looked reasonable last week. Again, fading Josh Allen with a 1-8 team is not pleasant, but point spreads exist for a reason.

    Recent findings suggest that the Ravens are theoretically desperate, but weren't they desperate in Week 10 and the few weeks before that? Maybe Baltimore just isn't good. Jacoby Brissett brings a level of competence to the offense but it wasn't even good enough to beat the winless Chargers on Monday night. The Panthers aren't great either, but they're better than this version of the Ravens.

    In a recent development, this is not a great week for NFL matchups. Some of these huge spreads will lead to blowouts. This seems like a good candidate. The Bears are coming off a bye and we know they can put up points in a hurry. Meanwhile, there's no real evidence the Saints are any good on either side of the ball (27th in offensive DVOA, 29th in defensive DVOA).

    Recent findings suggest that always beware a good team that is coming off being embarrassed. We can argue how good the Steelers really are, but they're 6-3 and practically a playoff lock. And there's no question they were embarrassed at Cincinnati. The Eagles have failed to cover in eight of nine games this season and while that's not necessarily predictive, we all have seen the 2026 Eagles play.

    According to recent reports, what were we just saying about this week's matchups? These teams have combined for three wins, and one of them came way back in Week 1 by the Jets. The Jets are coming off two straight blowout losses but those were against the Chiefs and Bills. The Chargers aren't really back just because they finally won a game. In a weird way, it could be a letdown spot after winning their first game. Either way, please don't spend time watching this game.

    The Jaguars are pretty good at blowing out bad teams. In five of their nine games this season they have won by 17 or more points. And this week they get a boost from trade acquisitions Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III making their Jacksonville debuts. Perhaps it's unfair to list the Giants as a bad team, but they're certainly on a different tier than the Jaguars.

    Sources indicate that we know the deal with the Broncos. They play close games, and find a way to win them. Over their last 20 games, including the postseason, Denver has two double-digit wins: over the Chargers when Los Angeles sat everyone in Week 18 last season, and against the Cardinals in Week 7. This is a tough matchup for Fernando Mendoza, but Las Vegas should be able to keep it within 10 points. Everyone else does against the Broncos.

    Behold, the one marquee matchup of Week 11! It's a really fun one. Kyle Shanahan's surgical offense vs. Brian Flores' blitz circus is fascinating. There is a pretty short list of reliable Super Bowl contenders and both of these teams should be on it, after we saw Kirk Cousins provide some stability to Minnesota's offense. Nobody has solved the Vikings' defense yet this season. The Packers moved the ball the best of any Vikings opponents back in Week 1, but we saw how the rematch went last week. Minnesota's defense is so good it held the Bears to three points back in Week 2 (Caleb Williams wasn't hurt in that game until midway through the fourth quarter). Let's take the points and see if Shanahan has the answer to Flores' defense.

    Joe Burrow is the hottest quarterback in the NFL and on his way to an MVP. Every time out he seems like a threat to have a 500-yard game. In other words, it's scary to fade him right now. But the Commanders are coming off some extra rest, they should feel reborn a bit by beating the Giants to stay somewhat alive in the NFC East race, and Jayden Daniels is still capable of keeping Washington in the game.

    #38662. National League Reliever of the Year: Matt Snyder explains his 2026 BBWAA ballot

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1023 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    National League Reliever of the Year: Matt Snyder explains his 2026 BBWAA ballot

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that mason Miller of the Padres won the 2026 National League Reliever of the Year award on Wednesday evening.
    • Industry observers note that first off, I didn't even bother to look at win-loss record.
    • It has been revealed that what makes the best relievers?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that mason Miller of the Padres won the 2026 National League Reliever of the Year award on Wednesday evening. That wasn't all too surprising, but I still wanted to explain the thought process behind my ballot. This was an honor, as it was the first-ever Baseball Writers' Association of America award for a relief pitcher. Yes, there have been plenty of reliever awards over the years, but this was the first year the BBWAA handed out such hardware.

    According to recent reports, 1. Mason Miller, Padres2. Jhoan Duran, Phillies3. Adrián Morejón, Padres4. Trevor Megill, Brewers5. Mason Montgomery, Pirates.

    And now here's how it unfolded on my end.

    Industry observers note that first off, I didn't even bother to look at win-loss record. It's a flawed enough stat these days with any individual player, but we really shouldn't be judging relievers by it. I'm also not worried about team performance here, as this is an individual award and we don't even need to wrestle with the word "valuable" being in the title like some MVP voters might. This is simply, "Who was the best relief pitcher in the league?".

    It has been revealed that what makes the best relievers? Run prevention (ERA, FIP, xFIP, etc.) matters, as does keeping runners off base (WHIP). It's helpful not only to the defense to strike hitters out, but it can also help a reliever bail out his team, so that's going to matter. Workload matters as well, as a reliever eating up as many outs as possible is very valuable to a team. I didn't factor saves as much as keeping leads (blown saves can hurt). Something I find helpful in judging relievers is win probability added. A reliever blowing games is going to be dinged in a substantial way, while closing down tougher games (one-run leads as opposed to three) is going to score extra via this measure. It's trickier with relievers, but WAR can help tell a story here, too.

    Sources indicate that finally, I have no doubt there was some eye test involved. That is, when I'm watching a game, which reliever coming out of the bullpen feels the most imposing to the opposition. Miller, Duran and Megill especially got bonus points here.

    A quick rundown of the major stats I examined follows.

    Among NL relievers, Miller was the best in ERA (1.67), xERA, FIP, xFIP and several other categories. Duran was second in ERA (and xERA, FIP and xFIP) with Yuki Matsui third, Brandyn Garcia fourth and Abner Uribe fifth. Megill was third in FIP, while Montgomery was third in xFIP and Morejón was fourth.

    In terms of keeping runners off base, Garcia led NL relievers in WHIP; Megill was second, Miller third, Duran ninth and Montgomery 10th.

    Kudos to Garcia for the excellent season, but his workload (51 ⅓ innings) dinged him a bit. Speaking of, Morejón worked 86 innings compared to 70 from Miller, 63 ⅔ from Montgomery, 61 ⅔ from Megill and 59 ⅓ from Duran.

    That noted, Garcia, Matsui and Uribe are firmly in the mix through these categories.

    Recent findings suggest that miller crushes here. He struck out 129 hitters, giving him 16.6 K/9 and a 47.4 K%. Montgomery was second in strikeout rate at 37.7%. Yes, it was that much of a blowout for Miller. Duran was third at 35.6%. Garcia was sixth, Morejón ninth, Megill 14th, Uribe 25th and Matsui 28th.

    According to recent reports, miller tied for the league lead in saves with Riley O'Brien. I never considered O'Brien, as his ERA was north of 4.00.

    It has been revealed that miller was also 38 of 41 in save chances. Duran was 33 of 35. Megill had 30 saves and seven holds with only three blown saves. Montgomery had 18 saves and nine holds with three blown saves. Morejón blew five saves, but he had three saves and 28 holds with an awful lot of multi-inning appearances. Uribe had six saves and 23 holds with two blown saves. Garcia? Stellar. He closed down five saves and 18 holds without ever blowing a lead. Matsui never blew a lead either, but he only had one save and 10 holds, meaning he wasn't tasked with much in the way of high-leverage innings. Being teammates with Miller and Morejón (and Jasaon Adam and Bradgley Rodríguez) will do that. As such, along with his relatively low strikeout rate, we can safely eliminate Matsui.

    By the time I've gotten here, I have seven players for five spots: Miller, Morejón, Duran, Megill, Montgomery, Uribe and Garcia.

    Using the FanGraphs calculation, Miller leads the way by a country mile at 3.7. Duran is second at 2.9, with Morejón at 2.8 and Megill at 2.5. Montgomery is eighth, Uribe ninth and Garcia, due in part to the workload concern, down at 17th.

    Over on Baseball Reference's version, Duran actually leads the way at 3.4. Miller is next at 3.1, followed by Montgomery (2.4) and Uribe (2.3). Megill sits at 1.7 while both Morejón and Garcia are at 1.9.

    In WPA, yes, Miller leads the way again at 4.56. Uribe is second at 3.49, with Morejón third at 3.23, Montgomery fourth at 2.86, Megill seventh, Garcia eighth and Duran 11th.

    Miller in first place wasn't all too difficult. He was the best relief pitcher in baseball in 2026 and checked every single box.

    According to recent reports, I had trouble with Duran over Morejón, while Megill and Montgomery were also very close in that group, as were Uribe and Garcia. I ended up leaning on Duran's high strikeout rate and excellent run prevention, which helped clear the way for his lead in WAR. Morejón's workload meant I couldn't go any lower than third with him, given how many crucial outs he soaked up for the Padres. Megill's regular-season numbers were better than Uribe's, notably the under-the-hood numbers, even if they were very close. And Montgomery was an absolute beast for the Pirates.

    It was incredibly tough to leave Uribe off, and Garcia was my hard-luck seventh-place finisher here when I had only five spots on my ballot.

    Industry News: Padres' Mason Miller, Blue Jays' Louis Varland named MLB Relievers of the Year in first-ever BBWAA award

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award.
    • The BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively.
    • Like the other BBWAA awards, the fresh Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award. The BBWAA introduced the award this year and, moving forward, will hand it out annually along with Rookies and Managers of the Year, Cy Young, and MVPs.

    The BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively. The Rivera and Hoffman Awards replaced the Delivery Man of the Year Award in 2015 and are voted on by a panel of former relievers, including Rivera and Hoffman.

    Like the other BBWAA awards, the fresh Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

    The best closer in baseball is the first-ever BBWAA National League Reliever of the Year. Miller was overwhelming from start to finish this past season, pitching to a 1.67 ERA with 129 strikeouts in only 70 innings. He led all pitchers with 3.9 WAR, well ahead of second-place Louie Varland (3.1 WAR), and he led the NL in saves (38) and games finished (57).

    Miller's strikeout rate lapped the field. Here are the highest strikeout rates (strikeouts per batter faced) among qualified relievers:.

    According to recent reports, miller just completed his first full season with the Padres. He was acquired from the Athletics at the 2025 trade deadline at a very high cost: San Diego sent shortstop Leo De Vries, one of the best prospects in baseball, to the A's in the six-player deal. Miller has been worth the price, though. He owns a 1.45 ERA in parts of two seasons with the Padres.

    In a recent development, this is the first major award of Miller's career, who finished fourth in the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year voting and has two All-Star Game selections (2024 and 2026), but otherwise had never received Cy Young or MVP votes prior to this season. He beat out the Brewers' Trevor Megill and Phillies' Jhoan Duran for the award.

    Sources indicate that after jumping into the national spotlight with his high usage during the 2025 postseason, Varland is the first winner of the BBWAA American League Reliever of the Year award. His 1.27 ERA led qualified relievers and his 3.1 WAR was tops in the AL. Varland struck out 87 batters in 78 innings and was fifth with 35 saves. He won with his sheer dominance, not his saves total.

    Varland was a workhorse for the Blue Jays this year, much like he was last October. He finished second in saves of at least four outs during the regular season:.

    The Blue Jays acquired Varland from the Minnesota Twins, his hometown team, at the 2025 trade deadline. He struggled initially after the deal, posting a 4.94 ERA with Toronto after the deadline, but Varland found his footing in the postseason and then found another gear in 2026. He was one of the game's best relievers and a true workhorse.

    Sources indicate that varland was an All-Star for the first time this season. This was also his first year receiving any award votes. He beat out the Guardians' Cade Smith and Rays' Bryan Baker for the award.

    According to recent reports, milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski has unanimously been named National League Cy Young Award winner for the 2026 Major League Baseball season. He beat out the Phillies' Cristopher Sánchez and the Braves' Chris Sale.

    According to recent reports, misiorowski takes home the honors of the Baseball Writers Association of America vote, which was revealed on Wednesday night. Misiorowski's triumph comes after a stellar age-24 season for the World Series champions:.

    Sources indicate that in addition to the top-line numbers above, Misiorowski struck out 37.9% of opposing batters, which is tops in all of MLB and a sky-scraping figure for any pitcher, let alone a starter. Miz also paced the majors in FIP with a mark of 2.17, and his ERA+ of 232 is the 13th-highest figure by a qualifier ever in MLB. Misiorowski's WAR of 6.4 ranked third in the NL behind Sánchez and Jesús Luzardo of the Philadelphia Phillies.

    Industry observers note that misiorowski was perhaps even more notable for his blazing fastball than he was the dominance of his statistical outputs. For the season, Misiorowski averaged 100.6 mph with his heavily used four-seamer, and on multiple occasions during 2026 he threw the fastest pitch on record, including this 105.5 mph offering from June:.

    105.5 MPH FROM JACOB MISIOROWSKI 🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/wjvkdc7iWE.

    While Misiorowski's playoff performance was not part of the Cy Young criteria – ballots are submitted before the playoffs begin – he did post a 1.89 ERA in four starts this postseason for the Brewers, who wound up winning it all for the first time in franchise history.

    It has been revealed that misiorowski is now the fourth Brewer to win the Cy Young Award. Corbin Burnes won in 2021, and Pete Vuckovich and Rollie Fingers won in 1982 and 1981, respectively, when the franchise was part of the American League.

    Sources indicate that given his level of dominance and relative youth, Misiorowski figures to enter the 2027 season as the odds-on favorite to win the hardware again. If he does, he'll become the first back-to-back Cy Young winner in the NL since Jacob deGrom of the Latest York Mets in 2018 and 2019.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, to no one's real surprise, Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers and Cam Schlittler of the Fresh York Yankees have been named the 2026 Cy Young Award winners for, respectively, the National League and American League.
    • Obviously, Cy Young winners have necessarily authored excellent seasons, but in the case of this year's winners, the descriptor "excellent" doesn't quite rise to meet the work of Misiorowski and Schlittler:.
    • According to recent reports, we could get into stuff, yes, as each has a blazing fastball that overwhelms hitters at the front end of a deep repertoire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, to no one's real surprise, Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers and Cam Schlittler of the Fresh York Yankees have been named the 2026 Cy Young Award winners for, respectively, the National League and American League. Each was confirmed as the winner of Major League Baseball's topmost honor for pitchers, and each won the balloting in unanimous fashion. They are the first duo to win unanimously in the same year in their respective leagues since Justin Verlander and Sandy Alcantara in 2022 and just the third in MLB history.

    Obviously, Cy Young winners have necessarily authored excellent seasons, but in the case of this year's winners, the descriptor "excellent" doesn't quite rise to meet the work of Misiorowski and Schlittler:.

    According to recent reports, we could get into stuff, yes, as each has a blazing fastball that overwhelms hitters at the front end of a deep repertoire. This exercise, though, is more about how Misiorowski and Schlittler have overwhelmed the opposition when it comes to keeping runs off the board. You'll note all the strikeouts above, of course, but what may catch the eye is that each boasts a sub-2.00 ERA. That's a time-honored signifier of pitcher impeccability, even if ERA has its flaws.

    In a recent development, to upgrade this familiar stat just a bit – and to put the two 2026 Cy Young winners' accomplishments into fitting context – we'll turn to ERA+. ERA+ is ERA adjusted to reflect league and home ballpark tendencies. An ERA+ of 100 represents the league average, and each point above or below that mark reflects a one-point change. For example, a pitcher with an ERA+ of 120 had a park- and league-adjusted ERA that was 20% better than the league average, while a pitcher with an ERA+ of 95 was 5% worse than the league average. So from the hurlers' standpoint, the higher the ERA+, the better.

    This is all a necessary step when comparing pitchers across eras, because run–scoring environments have changed so drastically over the history of the sport. For example, Pedro Martinez's ERA of 1.74 in 2000, when teams were averaging more than five runs per game, means a lot more than, say, Charlie Chech's 1.74 ERA in 1908, when teams averaged 3.38 runs per game. That's where ERA+ comes in. Martinez in 2000 had an ERA+ of 291, or a park-adjusted ERA that was 191% (!) better than the league average. Chech in 1908 had the same ERA as Martinez in 2000, but his ERA+ of 136 was drastically worse.

    As for the two moundsmen of present interest, Misiorowski this past season had an ERA+ of 232, which led the majors. Schlittler had an ERA+ of 215, which led the American League. Yes, they had those sub-2.00 ERAs, but, really, topping a 200 ERA+ is a much more impressive achievement. Counting Misiorowski and Schlittler but throwing out the pitchers who achieved the mark in the 60-game 2020 season (you should always throw out 2020), just 43 pitchers in MLB since 1900 have managed a 200 ERA+ or better across a qualifying number of innings. Over that same span and with 2020 also omitted, 201 pitchers have achieved a sub-2.00 ERA in a qualifying number of innings.

    As you can imagine, it's a rarity to have not one but two pitchers in the same season who have a 200 ERA+ or better, as was the case this past season with Misiorowski and Schlittler. How rare? No season has ever given us more than two such qualifiers. Here's the full list of those across all of modern MLB history (i.e., since 1900):.

    Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers (232); Cam Schlittler, Yankees (215).

    Jacob deGrom, Mets (218); Blake Snell, Rays (217).

    Jake Arrieta, Cubs (215), Zack Greinke, Dodgers (222).

    Roger Clemens, Blue Jays (222); Pedro Martinez, Expos (219).

    Carl Lundgren, Cubs (211); Jack Pfiester, Cubs (214).

    Christy Mathewson, Giants (233); Ed Reulbach, Cubs (209).

    Yes, just six seasons have given us more than one 200 ERA+ pitcher, and this year's Miz-Cam combo marks just the third time that we've had one from each league. Accordingly, this marks just the third time that each Cy Young winner has reached the 200 ERA+ benchmark in a given season.

    There's another, even more exclusive group that puts the Miz-Cam tandem in the proper context and hints at a future that's as bright as their present and their recent past. In 2026, Schlittler was in his age-25 campaign, while Misiorowski was in his age-24 season. So they're young as frontline aces go, and while you never want to make assumptions about pitcher health and durability in the current era, this duo's elite performance at both top-line and underlying level raises the possibility that each will win another Cy or two (or three) in the years to come.

    Turning back to the 200 ERA+ defining stat, such youth in tandem with such excellence is all but unprecedented. Of the seasons listed just above, just 1905 featured two pitchers who, like Miz and Cam this past season, were age 25 or younger at the time. Mathewson, the inner-circle all-time great, was 24 that season and Reulbach was a 22-year-old rookie. We haven't seen something like that in more than 120 years.

    Recent findings suggest that let's also note that Misiorowski and Shlittler, who each struck out more than 30% of opposing batters this season, absolutely have the stuff and foundational, forward-looking results to continue lording over their guild. Until that comes to pass, though, let's appreciate ther historical rare success and their even more historically rare combination of success and youth.

    Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Newly introduced Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams declared the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.
