He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Fresh Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Newly introduced Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    According to recent reports, for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a newly introduced era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Goaltending has been an matter in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a substantial reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Recent findings suggest that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Latest Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    It has been revealed that in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    According to recent reports, hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    Industry observers note that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    Sources indicate that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    In a recent development, that said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    Industry observers note that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Industry observers note that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Recent findings suggest that daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his fresh team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you simply looked at his touchdown total, you'd think that Derrick Henry had himself a night in the Week 10 finale.
    • It has been revealed that well, when you zoom out of the mere touchdown total, you'll find Henry and the Baltimore Ravens ground attack managing just 16 total rushing yards amid a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night.
    • Recent findings suggest that "What were they doing?" Henry asked when questioned about how L.A.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you simply looked at his touchdown total, you'd think that Derrick Henry had himself a night in the Week 10 finale. The veteran back once again barreled into the end zone multiple times, and even tied LaDainian Tomlinson for the most seasons with at least 10 rushing touchdowns (9) in NFL history. Not too shabby, right?

    It has been revealed that well, when you zoom out of the mere touchdown total, you'll find Henry and the Baltimore Ravens ground attack managing just 16 total rushing yards amid a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night. That led to Henry getting a bit testy in the locker room following the loss that dragged Baltimore to 4-6 on the season and its fifth straight defeat.

    Recent findings suggest that "What were they doing?" Henry asked when questioned about how L.A. was stopping them on the ground, via the Baltimore Banner. "Not letting us run the ball. We weren't efficient enough to run the ball. They were better on that side.".

    When asked whether it was more about the Ravens not executing or the Chargers doing a good job at stopping them, Henry remarked, "Everything. Just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game. 16 total yards is a clear explanation.".

    According to recent reports, those 16 rushing yards are the third-fewest in a game in team history. They had zero rushing yards in the entire first half. As for Henry, he accounted for 10 of those 16 rushing yards on 10 attempts. When accounting for his five receptions in the loss, Henry averaged just 1.3 yards per touch, which is the fewest this season of any player (233 instances) that has had at least 15 touches in a game.

    Industry observers note that this lackluster ground attack on Monday night isn't a one-off for Baltimore. The run game has been virtually nonexistent amid this losing streak, which coincides with Lamar Jackson missing time due to an ankle and right thumb injury. Over the past seven games, Henry has logged zero 20-plus-yard rushes and has failed to have a 10-yard rush in three of his last four games.

    In a recent development, during this five-game losing skid without Jackson, Henry has logged 81 touches for 246 yards. That 3.0 yards-per-touch average is the fewest of any player in a five-game span in the past five seasons (min. 80 touches), according to CBS Sports Research.

    Again, this has a lot more to do with Lamar Jackson's absence than with Henry falling off. When you subtract Jackson from the equation, it takes the mystery out of Baltimore's running game. No defense fears the like of Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano or Jacoby Brissett pulling the ball from Henry and running it himself as they do with Jackson. That allows them to key in on Henry and the ground game even more, especially if they're struggling in the passing attack.

    Here's a look at Baltimore's remaining opponents and how they are against the run so far this season:.

    According to recent reports, the Ravens are 4-6 on the season and situated as the No. 10 seed in the AFC playoff picture, looking up at the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and New England Patriots (5-5) in the wild card race. They are all looking to unseat either the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) or Cleveland Browns (6-4), who hold the No. 6 and No. 7 seeds entering Week 11.

    If Baltimore can't find a way to rekindle their ground attack, their season may go by the wayside with it and eliminate any reason for Lamar Jackson to return from IR once his broken right thumb heals.

    • Joseph has been out the entire season with a knee injury sustained last year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is on the verge of returning to the lineup. Lions head coach Dan Campbell noted during a radio interview on Tuesday that "the blueprint would be to get [Joseph] going this week" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, according to The Detroit Free Press.

    Joseph has been out the entire season with a knee injury sustained last year. He played in only the first six games of the 2025 season before being placed on injured reserve. Joseph dealt with the knee injury during the 2025 preseason and played through it early in the year, but he aggravated it and missed the remainder of the year.

    In a recent development, the Lions' defense desperately needs the lift that Joseph can provide on the back end after losing star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL suffered in the team's victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye on the first drive of the game and then injured his knee while celebrating the play.

    In a recent development, detroit's defense has played better of late after beginning the season looking like one of the worst units in the league. The Lions allowed at least 24 points in each of their first four games and at least 30 points in three of them. They also allowed at least 335 yards in each of those games and at least 445 in three of them. Since that point, they have yet to allow more than 21 points or 327 yards, and they have won five straight games.

    It's probably no coincidence that they recently got defensive back Brian Branch back from his injury to solidify one of the spots in the secondary, which has helped limit opponents' ability to attack through the air. The Lions have been excellent against the run during that stretch, though, and their ability to wrangle opponents' run games may now take a hit with Hutchinson out. So, they need the lift that Joseph will provide on the back end to make up for it.

    Detroit's schedule for the rest of the season includes a few tough tests, such as the division rival Bears twice and the Packers in the regular-season finale. However, it also provides some easier games against the Buccaneers (possibly without Baker Mayfield), Falcons, Titans, Vikings and Giants. Joseph's return will surely help them navigate that slate, even if he has to ramp up to a full workload of snaps.

    #38647. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4993 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” mentioned head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    Industry observers note that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the latest season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

    Industry observers note that tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

    Industry observers note that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    It has been revealed that spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Industry observers note that brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews stated: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    We're in the throes of spooky season, and fittingly, the New Jersey Devils just got a lot scarier with the acquisition of superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.

    One of the best goaltenders in the world, Hellebuyck fills the biggest need on the Devils roster. With him in between the pipes and an electrifying group of forwards, Upcoming Jersey will be a force in the Eastern Conference.

    In a recent development, don't take my word for it. Just look at what the Devils did Tuesday against the Dallas Stars. In his first start with the team, Hellebuyck stopped 17 of the 18 shots he faced -- allowing one goal on 2.04 expected goals against -- in a 5-1 victory.

    Recent findings suggest that nico Hischier, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes each had multi-point nights as the Devils took full advantage of the chances they created against a stout Dallas team. This type of game has to be exactly what general manager Sunny Mehta envisioned when he swung the deal for Hellebuyck.

    Industry observers note that moving forward, the Devils will be burdened with the pressure that comes along with being a bona fide Cup contender. For a franchise that's fallen short of expectations a few times lately, that can be a scary prospect, and it inspired a special Halloween edition of the NHL Power Rankings in which I highlight the scariest thing about each team.

    When the Cleveland Browns traded their best player -- one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, no less -- this offseason, nobody expected them to be any good.

    When they named a starting quarterback who was feuding with his own fans and had been arguably the worst acquisition in pro sports history, nobody expected them to be any good.

    According to recent reports, when they opened the season with a 34-10 loss, the sentiment was the same as it had always been. "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster, the Browns is the Browns," Mike Tomlin, the longtime coach of the AFC North-rival Steelers, stated in his NBC debut.

    It has been revealed that nine weeks later, the Browns are very much not those Browns. Cleveland is 6-4 after erasing a 17-point deficit in a crucial Week 10 win over the Texans. If the playoffs started today, the Browns would be in them as the AFC's No. 7 seed.

    Teams are what their records say they are, but context is notable, too. All six of Cleveland's wins have come by one score, tied with the Broncos for most in the league. Cleveland ranks 21st in point margin this season (-32). But even more than that ...

    But, again, the record is the record. Just hear Todd Monken tell it.

    "Isn't that cool? Isn't that awesome?" Monken mentioned after the win. "I mean, holy shit. There's no other way to put it, man. You're 6-4 ... and our guys continue to fight, and we're 6-2 in one-score games. Indicates a lot about our guys, man.".

    Industry observers note that it certainly does. Now, as the Browns hit their bye week, the question is whether they can sustain it.

    In a recent development, the ability to win close games is a crucial one in the NFL, but relying on it too much can put you in a lot of trouble. The Browns have faced a lot of trouble this year; just re-read the third bullet point above.

    Recent findings suggest that but that's when Deshaun Watson has stepped in. His six game-winning drives are tied for most by any quarterback through a team's first 10 games since at least 1950 -- and that's despite him missing one game, too.

    Some team-wide stats can convolute how a quarterback actually plays, but Watson has indeed taken his play to an absurd level on these game-winning drives.

    In a recent development, add that up, and that's 23 for 29 (79% completion percentage) for 254 yards, which is 8.8 yards per attempt. He made another significant-time throw Sunday to set up Quinshon Judkins' winning touchdown.

    Recent findings suggest that harold Fannin Jr. down to the 5!HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQL0DtQAaV.

    Watson has been, generally, average this season. He takes too many sacks, and the down-to-down accuracy is iffy at best. He has thrown just four touchdowns compared to seven interceptions. That combination can snowball, and it has in Cleveland's three losses with him under center. But let Cleveland hang around long enough, and Watson has proved to be excellent late in games.

    "I wish we could find ways to pull it out a little bit sooner so we don't have to go through that," Watson remarked. "But, whatever it takes to win. Whatever it takes to stay on the winning side is the biggest thing.".

    Recent findings suggest that when Watson and the offense struggle, the defense does enough to keep the Browns within striking distance. In all six Browns wins this year, their opponent has scored 24 or fewer points.

    Recent findings suggest that cleveland has been excellent against the pass this year -- only the Vikings have a better defensive passing success rate -- and generally solid overall. The Browns can get gashed by the run and give up some big plays, but they also make enough big stops to hold on. The Browns are first in the percentage of plays that go for zero or negative yards and first in fourth-down conversion rate allowed. They're also eighth in red-zone touchdown rate allowed. Those are all vital for a team that can struggle to score.

    Industry observers note that when the Browns are trailing in the second half of games this year, they rank fifth in defensive EPA per play. On the season, they're 11th. Again: a unit coming up biggest in the biggest moments.

    The Browns are just the sixth team since 2000 -- and the first since the 2017 Titans -- to have at least 6 wins through 10 games despite having a -30 or worse season point differential. Here's how those six teams finished:.

    6+ wins, -30 or worse point diff through 10 games since 2000.

    To narrow it down even more, only four teams since 2000 have had six game-winning drives in their first 10 games. Two of them -- the Browns and the Broncos -- are from this year. The other two are the 2016 Lions, who went 9-7 and missed the playoffs, and the 2003 Panthers, who went 11-5 and made the Super Bowl.

    According to recent reports, so, yes, these teams that outplay their point differential can and often do make the postseason. Furthermore, it's key to remember that none of those teams had the 14-team playoff. Right now, that expanded field is playing a crucial role.

    According to recent reports, that's the first piece of good news for the Browns. Another is that the AFC playoff race doesn't look especially cutthroat. The Patriots may not have Drake Maye again this season. Same for the Ravens and Lamar Jackson. The Browns' win over the Texans might be the nail in the coffin for 3-6 Houston, which has no room for error and now trails the head-to-head against Cleveland.

    SportsLine projections have the Browns winning 9.4 games, seventh-most in the AFC and well clear of the closest competitor, the Texans at 8.0.

    That leaves Cleveland with a 68% chance to make the postseason, per SportsLine calculations. The Texans and Patriots (19% each) are far, far behind.

    It has been revealed that of course, nothing is set in stone. It's only been 10 weeks. Cleveland still has tough tests left, and the Browns have struggled against even some of the league's worst teams.

    For now, this high-wire escape act is working, and the answer for "Can they keep this up?" is an unequivocal "Yes.".

    Unless one of the less-than-inspiring teams behind them makes a push, the Browns are on track to be, based on preseason expectations, of the most unlikely playoff teams of the 21st century -- a true credit to Monken, Watson and the entire organization.

    And as Watson stated Sunday, "Once you get in, anything can happen.".

    Smart and Bassey had gotten tangled up on the other end. After they disconnected and Bassey made his way back on defense, Smart chased after Bassey from behind, made contact, swung around to his front side, and threw the blow that is likely going to lead to a suspension.

    According to recent reports, smart was hit with a flagrant-2 foul, which carries an automatic ejection (the 13th of Smart's career). Smart didn't stick around long after he threw the punch. As players were being separated to keep things from escalating any further, Smart almost immediately took off his elbow sleeve and walked straight to the locker room. He knew he was gone.

    As for Bassey's side of the story, the Warriors' significant man mentioned Smart was "playing dirty" all night.

    Recent findings suggest that "He's been playing dirty the whole game," Bassey said. "In the first half, I was trying to set a screen and he grabbed my knee. So I mean, he was playing dirty. [On the play in question], I think I was trying to get a rebound and he was grabbing my hand and I was trying to run back on defense. ... And then he got up on me and swung. Obviously that was weak. I think that was, honestly, fake toughness.".

    Asked whether he said anything to Smart to set him off, Bassey explained: "He said something to me. He said something like, 'Hey, don't do that.' I said, 'Do what?' It's a grown-man's league.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Dallas Cowboys may be on the verge of their fifth defensive coordinator in five seasons by the time the 2027 NFL season kicks off next year.
    • According to recent reports, after having top-five and top-10 ranked defenses under Dan Quinn from 2021 to 2023, Dallas' defensive coordinator position appears to be cursed, possibly as cursed as Hogwarts' Defense Against the Dark Arts professor in Harry Potter.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Dallas Cowboys may be on the verge of their fifth defensive coordinator in five seasons by the time the 2027 NFL season kicks off next year.

    According to recent reports, after having top-five and top-10 ranked defenses under Dan Quinn from 2021 to 2023, Dallas' defensive coordinator position appears to be cursed, possibly as cursed as Hogwarts' Defense Against the Dark Arts professor in Harry Potter. Mike Zimmer filled in as the last defensive coordinator on Mike McCarthy's Cowboys staff in 2024. Matt Eberflus floundered in his one season as DC on current Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer's first staff in Dallas.

    Current defensive coordinator Christian Parker, the former Philadelphia Eagles defensive pass game coordinator who is in his first DC job at the age of 34, isn't performing much differently from Eberflus despite the Cowboys pouring in significant free-agent and draft capital into the unit. Dallas is 4-6 in 2026 with the No. 5 scoring offense (28.6 points per game) and the No. 30 scoring defense (28.2 points per game) in the NFL this season.

    That is why Jerry Jones felt comfortable floating the idea of a change at Dallas' defensive coordinator position once again.

    "We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about that here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, via The Dallas Morning News.

    Recent findings suggest that in the team's 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers — the NFC's No. 1 seed — in Week 10, the Cowboys defense allowed 584 total yards, the most allowed in a home game in franchise history.

    Recent findings suggest that the 49ers also became the first team in NFL history with three touchdowns of 50-plus yards by players age 30 and older. San Francisco wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who will be 31 years old soon, ripped off a 70-yard rushing touchdown on an end-around play in which he was nowhere near getting touched. Running back Christian McCaffrey, who is 30 years old, totaled both a 66-yard receiving touchdown and a 74-yard receiving touchdown. McCaffrey's 66-yarder came on an all-out blitz from Parker that forced 37-year-old edge rusher Von Miller to cover the All-Pro running back.

    Industry observers note that jones also made it sound like he has a lot of faith in Parker, and that the youngest defensive coordinator in franchise history just needs more time and/or seasoning to call plays. That's despite the Cowboys having the league's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).

    Industry observers note that "Everything about him would give you promise that he would be an excellent play caller. Everything," Jones remarked Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "He has outstanding people skills, and communication and relationships with players. Those are key things now. They make a substantial difference. Some of the best coaches you'll ever see have had their turn and had to take another run on it in play calling.".

    Third down conversion rate allowed.

    Schottenheimer and Dallas' players may not hold the same faith in Parker at the moment. The Cowboys head coach was asked at his Monday press conference if the locker room still has confidence in Parker, and he didn't exactly leap to his defensive coordinator's defense.

    Sources indicate that "Still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said on Monday. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. We're taking a deep dive and looking at everything.".

    When directly asked whether he is considering a change at his defensive coordinator position, he did not offer a vote of confidence.

    According to recent reports, "I'm not saying that," Schottenheimer remarked when asked if a DC change was possible. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two days after losing by 51 points to the Golden State Warriors, the New Orleans Pelicans managed an even more embarrassing loss on Wednesday when they were blown out 145-111 by the Brooklyn Nets, who were 2-8 entering the night.

    Fresh Orleans (4-8) began the season on a four-game losing streak before bouncing back to .500 with a four-game winning streak, but has now lost four straight again. The concerning part of their recent skid is that the Pelicans have grown increasingly uncompetitive.

    Sources indicate that in that initial four-game losing streak to open the season, the Pelicans lost by a combined 23 points in the four games. In their last two games, they've lost by a combined 85 points, leaving Zion Williamson with just one word to describe his team's effort.

    "Unacceptable," Williamson said, via ESPN. "I don't even have a lot of words. Just unacceptable.".

    In a recent development, williamson called out the Pelicans' defensive effort during this latest losing streak, as they've allowed at least 138 points in three consecutive games. The seventh-year star then called for his team to look inward and be honest with themselves about whether they're doing everything they can to help the team win.

    "I noted nobody likes to lose like this, but if we don't like to lose like this, we have to start with ourselves first," Williamson said. "Look in the mirror and say, did I do what I needed to do for my team? Not individually. Did I do what I needed to do for my team? And then we go from there.".

    It's never a good sign when a team's star is questioning the collective's effort level and commitment to winning just 12 games into the season. This is when buy-in should be the easiest to get because a team's goals are still right in front of them, but the Pelicans are already showing signs that they will likely spend another season at the bottom of the Western Conference.

    That four-game winning streak -- which was somewhat schedule-aided with two games against the woeful Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz -- feels like ages ago for the Pelicans. If they're going to turn things around, Williamson is right that it starts with accountability from the players, but with some key injuries to Trey Murphy III and Yves Missi, coupled with poor play, this season could get away from Fresh Orleans quickly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.
    • Sources indicate that an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team confirmed that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
    • Industry observers note that the injury happened halfway through the first quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.

    Sources indicate that an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team confirmed that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks. While two weeks is the best-case scenario, that being just the re-evaluation point means his absence could extend beyond that timetable -- as that also doesn't include any ramp-up process he would need to clear before returning to the floor.

    Industry observers note that the injury happened halfway through the first quarter. You can see Curry get tangled up with Alperen Sengun and grab at his side after they separate.

    Steph Curry got injured after Sengun grabbed and twisted his arm pic.twitter.com/4p20Rogpeu.

    Moments later, Curry hit his lone 3-pointer of the game and could once again be seen grabbing at his side after the shot.

    Stephen Curry headed to the locker room with an apparent right hip injury. pic.twitter.com/1zVrNz00bH.

    Sources indicate that curry exited the game at the next dead ball and didn't return. After the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr remarked concern about Curry's injury was "high.".

    It has been revealed that "He remarked he tweaked something in his abdominal area," Kerr said. "He said he's never done it before. ... Concern is high, but I have no idea the extent of the injury.".

    In recent seasons, the range of recovery times for other notable NBA oblique injuries has varied.

    It's unclear how severe Curry's oblique tear is. These are all strains, which is code for a minor tear, but the worst-case scenario would be a more severe one. We saw this two years ago when the Orlando Magic lost both Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero to oblique tears that kept Banchero out for 10 weeks and Wagner for more than a month.

    Any extended absence would be disastrous for the Warriors, who are not equipped to cover for any Curry injury. Curry has gotten off to a scorching start, entering Wednesday averaging 30.1 points per game on 50.3/45.7/98.7 shooting splits with Golden State winning eight straight games for the first time since the 2022 championship season.

    Industry observers note that but this was always a fingers-crossed situation with an aging roster. Already down Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis, and with Brandon Williams and Gary Payton II also on the shelf and wing Will Richard playing through a ligament tear in his thumb, the Warriors have little, if any, margin for any more injuries.

    This comes at a particularly tough time for the Warriors, who are entering their most difficult stretch of the season. On Friday, they'll visit the San Antonio Spurs before facing the Dallas Mavericks and Fresh Orleans Pelicans on a back-to-back.

    The Warriors have opened up at 8-4 with a top-three offense, but that can go south very quickly without Curry.

    Curry is the latest NBA star to face an extended injury absence in the first month of the 2026-27 season. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren (Thunder), Anthony Edwards (Timberwolves), Tyrese Haliburton (Pacers), Kawhi Leonard (Raptors), Paolo Banchero (Magic), Jalen Duren (Pistons) and Kon Knueppel (Hornets) are among the players at the moment dealing with multi-week absences.

    • Recent findings suggest that over the next four weeks, Houston plays Indianapolis, the Baltimore Ravens, the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Washington Commanders.
    • Al-Shaair, a Pro-Bowler in 2025, has dealt with the groin injury all year, missing a pair of games with it so far this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Houston Texans are losing a key defensive piece for at least the next four games. Houston placed starting linebacker and team captain Azeez Al-Shaair on injured reserve, the team announced. Al-Shaair has been dealing with a groin injury that kept him out of Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns. The groin injury is significant enough that it requires surgery and he will likely miss more than four games, according to the Houston Chronicle.

    Recent findings suggest that over the next four weeks, Houston plays Indianapolis, the Baltimore Ravens, the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Washington Commanders. The Texans then close the season with a four-game stretch in which they play the Jacksonville Jaguars, Philadelphia Eagles, Green Bay Packers and Tennessee Titans.

    Al-Shaair, a Pro-Bowler in 2025, has dealt with the groin injury all year, missing a pair of games with it so far this season. He has recorded 68 tackles, one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits and three passes defensed in seven games.

    In Al-Shaair's absence, Jake Hansen will presumably see more snaps at linebacker (he played 66 of 68 defensive snaps against the Browns) while Henry To'oto'o will take over the green dot responsibilities of calling the defense, according to KPRC2.

    Industry observers note that the Texans' defense as a whole has been one of the more disappointing units in the NFL in 2026, ranking 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed, and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.

    It has been revealed that instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks this season, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. The Texans have also failed to force turnovers at the same rate as a year ago, with only 8.8% of opponents' drives resulting in a turnover (27th in the league) compared with 14.6% last season (fourth).

    Those relative struggles have led the Texans to compile a 3-6 record despite C.J. Stroud and the offense showing significant year-over-year improvement. The Texans are now 2.5 games back of the No. 7 seed in the AFC and need to go on a strong run down the stretch of the season to have any hope of making the playoffs. And now, they'll likely have to do it without one of the leaders of their defense.

    #38637. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1276 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.
    • There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.
    • Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    According to recent reports, there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    He's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    According to recent reports, we'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a upcoming procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    Industry observers note that I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    In a recent development, again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

    According to recent reports, for those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    Sources indicate that yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    Industry observers note that justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    According to recent reports, corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    It has been revealed that we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    Sources indicate that by this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Sources indicate that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    Sources indicate that it's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Recent findings suggest that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    We already know the Wild are significant-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    In a recent development, however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

    It has been revealed that carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    According to recent reports, allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Recent findings suggest that dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic newly introduced look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

    The Manchester City striker revealed his upcoming buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

    Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

    In a recent development, pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's latest haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

    Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

    Sources indicate that haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

    It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

    Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

    So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

    According to recent reports, “I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager stated. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many notable things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

    “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

    “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

    It has been revealed that maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

    “But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

    “The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

    “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

    #38634. Taxes hurt: Breaking down an NFL player's weekly pay stub and where all the money goes

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (464 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Taxes hurt: Breaking down an NFL player's weekly pay stub and where all the money goes

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (464 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that if you've ever wondered what an NFL player's paycheck looks like, we now know the answer thanks to Rashee Rice.
    • Recent findings suggest that the paycheck offers a rare inside look into where all the money goes for an NFL player.
    • Like the rest of us, Rice has to pay taxes and he also has to pay his NFLPA dues.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you've ever wondered what an NFL player's paycheck looks like, we now know the answer thanks to Rashee Rice. The Chiefs wide receiver recently filed for bankruptcy, and as part of the court filing, he had to include a copy of his pay stub that he gets from the team each week.

    Recent findings suggest that the paycheck offers a rare inside look into where all the money goes for an NFL player. Rice is at the moment in the fourth and final year of a rookie deal that's paying him $1.635 million in base salary this year, but when it comes to his take-home pay, it's much more complicated than just looking at his base salary.

    Like the rest of us, Rice has to pay taxes and he also has to pay his NFLPA dues. Not to mention, his paycheck is also being garnished to pay off several civil liabilities that he's facing.

    For the week of Oct. 19-25, Rice got paid $43,353.08, but he only got to take home a small portion of that.

    Let's take a look at where the money went.

    Here's a look at one of Rashee Rice's recent pay stubs from the Kansas City Chiefs (via his bankruptcy filing).$43,353 in weekly earnings- $19,570 for taxes/SS/Medicare- $9,117 for garnishments, union dues, and fines————= $14,665 in take-home payAs of October 25, Rice has… pic.twitter.com/dNjtBJaEVi.

    It's certainly interesting to see how little Rice ends up taking home here.

    After all the deductions were made, Rice's total net pay was $14,665.25. That means he only got to take home 33.9% of his paycheck. Most players don't have to deal with garnishments or fines, so let's take those out real quick. If Rice did NOT have to pay those two things, he still would have taken home only 52.7% of his paycheck ($22,860.96).

    Another interesting thing about this pay stub is that you can see all the ways a player gets paid besides their base salary. For instance, Rice has been paid over $350,000 in performance pay along with a $75,000 workout bonus this year. Rice also earned $20,500 just for attending training camp. A player's salary only applies to games they play in, but they still do earn a stipend for training camp. Under the current CBA, veterans get paid $3,500 per week during training camp and this pay is equal for everyone, so Patrick Mahomes and Rice would make the same amount.

    Although Rice is only making $43,000 per paycheck right now, that number will likely shoot up starting next year. The 26-year-old is in the final year of his rookie deal, and he'll definitely be cashing in this offseason, whether that's in free agency or signing an extension with the Chiefs.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas.
    • Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.
    • In a recent development, we have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

    Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

    In a recent development, we have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

    It has been revealed that phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

    The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a big bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

    The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

    Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

    The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

    The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

    As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

    Marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

    The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

    According to recent reports, happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

    The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

    Yesterday's substantial news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

    Bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

    Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

    May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He showed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

    Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that says a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

    Jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

    Much has been remarked and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

    As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

    DeLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

    Fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

    Sources indicate that "We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to.".

    Sources indicate that the Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

    So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

    #38629. Naz Reid landing spots: Four NBA contenders that make sense if Hornets look to move sharp-shooting substantial man
